Entries.Text: Collision Editor
Collision Editor
This tool is only supported for Dark Souls III, Sekiro, Elden Ring, Nightreign and Armored Core VI.
Reshape map collision by moving its vertices in the viewport. Edits are previewed until they are committed, which rebuilds the edited collision and writes it into the project.
Collision isn't loaded, so there is nothing to edit. Enable collision loading and load the map again.
Actions
Start or stop editing, and commit or discard the edits.
Start Collision Edit
Shows the cursor on the collision under the mouse, so its vertices can be moved with the keys below.
Stop Collision Edit
Hides the cursor. Edits that haven't been committed are kept, and can be committed or discarded later.
Commit Changes
Rebuilds the edited collision from the moved vertices and writes the collision binders it is in into the project. Can be undone.
Discard Changes
Puts every moved vertex back where it was.
Layer
The collision layer the cursor edits. Only this layer is hit, as the layers lie on top of each other.
High and low collision are the same ground at two levels of detail. Fall protection is a barrier of its own.
{0} collision isn't displayed, so the cursor can't be placed on it.
Display {0} Collision
Displays this collision layer for every collision part.
Linked Layers
Whether the other layer of a part follows the edits, so high and low collision stay on the same ground.
Link High and Low

Moves the vertices of the other layer near the edited vertex by the same amount, and commits both files. The layers don't share vertices, and don't always cover the same ground, so only vertices within the link distance follow. Works whether or not the other layer is displayed.
{0} collision isn't linked to another layer.
{0} collision follows edits to {1} collision.
Link Distance
How close the other layer's vertices must be to the edited vertex to follow it fully. Past it, the radius fades them out.
The distance in world units. In Stormveil, 94% of low vertices lie within 0.5 of the high collision; larger distances may pull in nearby surfaces that aren't the same ground.
Linked: {0}
Linked: none (this part has no other layer that can be edited)
Step
How far each press of the raise or lower key moves the vertex.
The distance in world units, up or down.
Radius
Moves the vertices around the target as well, less the further they are from it.
The distance in world units. 0 moves the target vertex alone.
Cursor Size
The size of the cursor sphere. The vertex marker is a little smaller.
The radius in world units.
Cursor Opacity
How solid the fill inside the cursor's wireframe is. Lower lets the collision under a large cursor show through.
0% leaves the wireframe alone; 100% fills the cursor solid.
Controls
The keys work while the mouse is over the viewport and no mouse button is held, as the mouse buttons fly the camera with the same keys. They can be changed in the keybind settings.
{0}: raise the vertex.
{0}: lower the vertex.
Hold {0}: drag the vertex across the ground at its height.
Cursor
The collision and vertex under the cursor.
Collision is hidden. It must be displayed to be edited.
Start editing to show the cursor.
Collision: {0} ({1})
Vertex {0}: {1}
Move the mouse over a collision to place the cursor.
Pending Edits
The collision files with moved vertices that haven't been committed.
No edits.
{0}: {1} vertices moved
Discarded the collision edits.
Failed to read the collision mesh of {0}.
{0} would have no triangles left, so nothing was committed.
Failed to rebuild the collision mesh of {0}, so nothing was committed.
Rebuilt a mesh of {0}: {1} triangles decoded, {2} kept, {3} vertices, {4} materials.
Committed the collision edits of {0}.
Committed the collision edits of {0}, but writing the collision binders failed. Save the map to try again.
The viewport couldn't redraw {0}. It shows the new shape once the map is loaded again.
Edit
Create
Fall Protection
Generate the fall protection collision of the selected collision part: flat vertical walls along the outer edges of its high or low collision, written into its fall protection (f) file.
Fall protection can only be generated for Elden Ring and Nightreign.
Collision Part
The collision part the walls are made for. They go in the f file of its model, which every part placing the model uses.
Select a single collision part to generate its fall protection.
{0} (model {1}, map {2})
{0} has no fall protection binder to put the walls in.
Source Layer
The collision whose outer edges the walls follow.
High or low collision of the part's model. The two usually cover the same ground.
The part's model has no {0} to follow.
The triangles of {0} couldn't be read.
Direction
Which outer edges get walls, by the way they face in the world.

All edges, or only those facing one way: north is +Z and east is +X, as the open world's map numbers go up. An edge faces away from the collision it is the edge of, and counts for the direction it is nearest.
All
North (+Z)
East (+X)
South (-Z)
West (-X)
Drop Edges
Whether only the outer edges that can be fallen off get walls.
Drop Edges Only

On, an outer edge gets a wall only if it is the edge of ground that can be stood on (facing up, slopes up to about 60 degrees) and, just past it, the ground of this part and the loaded collision parts around it is more than the minimum drop lower, or missing. Open seams between pieces of floor, and the edges of walls and ceilings, then get no walls. Off, every outer edge gets one.
How far below an edge the ground past it must be for the edge to be a drop, in world units. Ground up to 0.5 above the edge counts as ground too.
{0} of them are drops, with the collision of {1} other parts as ground.
No outer edge facing that way is a drop, so there is nothing to generate.
Wall Height
How far the walls reach above the edges they stand on.
In world units. Every wall in the game's fall protection is 1.8 high.
Collision Filter
The collision filter info of the wall bodies.
The game's walls use 0 or 1; Elden Ring's legacy dungeons only use 1. What the two values block isn't known.
Existing Walls
What happens to the walls the f file already has.
{0} has {1} wall bodies.
Keep Existing Walls
On, the new walls are added to the file's walls, e.g. to add one direction at a time. Off, they replace them.
Preview
The walls that will be generated, drawn in the viewport in the fall protection colour while this tab is open.
Show in Viewport
Draws the walls in the viewport, placed with the part. Collision must be shown in the viewport's filters.
{0} outer edges, {1} facing the direction: {2} walls in {3} bodies.
No outer edge faces that way, so there is nothing to generate.
Actions
Generate the walls.
Generate Fall Protection
Puts the walls in the part's f file (made if the model has none), as one action that can be undone, then writes the fall protection binder into the project.
{0} has no file to base a new fall protection file on. Nothing was generated.
{0} isn't a fall protection file that walls can be added to. Nothing was generated.
The walls of {0} couldn't be built. Nothing was generated.
Generated the walls of {0}, but writing the fall protection binder failed. Save the map to try again.
Generated {1} fall protection walls in {2} bodies into {0} ({3} bodies in the file).
Create a new collision for the active map: new files in its high and low collision binders, written into the project, and a collision part placing them.
Map
The map the collision is made for: the map the content tree shows, which follows the last selected object.
No map is active. Load a map, or select an object in one.
{0} has no high collision binder to add the collision to.
Shape
What the collision's mesh is.
A basic shape, placed at the placement orb, or the FLVERs of the selected map pieces and assets, combined where they are placed. The new part goes where the first of them, in map order, is.
Square
Triangle
Circle
Semi-Circle
Selected FLVERs
Select one or more map pieces or assets of the active map to use their FLVERs.
Facing
Which way the collision's faces point, as in the Havok Editor's collision generator.
Up for ground that is stood on. If the collision can be fallen through in game, try the other facing.
Collision Material
The collision material of the triangles. A FLVER mesh whose material is named hkm_Name_Property keeps that material.
Parameters
The size of the shape, in world units.
Width
The size of the square along X.
Length
The size of the square along Z.
Size
The length of the triangle's sides.
Radius
The distance from the centre to the edge.
Segments
How many triangles make up the curve. More is smoother.
Source: {0} ({1})
Sources: {0} parts. The collision is placed where {1} is.
None of the selected parts' FLVERs could be read.
The FLVER of {0} ({1}) couldn't be read, so it is left out.
Failed to read the FLVER of {0}.
Meshes
Which meshes of each FLVER go into the collision.
All
Use every mesh of every FLVER.
None
Use no meshes, to pick a few.
Model ID
The number of the new collision model: the part's model is h followed by it, and its files are named for it.
Six digits. Suggested as the first unused number after the map's highest below 900000.
The model ID must be six digits.
The map already has a collision {0}: its mesh will be overwritten, once confirmed.
Preview
The triangles the collision will have.
Triangles: {0}
Actions
Create the collision.
Create Collision

Adds the collision's files to the map's high and low collision binders, writes the binders into the project, and adds a collision part placing it. Undoing removes the part; the files stay in the binders.
{0} has no collision part to base the new part on.
The {0} binder has no collision file with a single compressed mesh to base the new file on.
Failed to build {0}, so nothing was created.
Failed to write the collision binders for collision {0}, so no part was added.
Created {0} ({1} triangles).
Overwrite Collision
The map already has this model. Asks to confirm, then gives its existing files the new mesh, makes any of its files the binders don't have, and writes the binders into the project.
Overwrite Collision
Overwrite the mesh of collision {0}?
{0}: its mesh is replaced. The body keeps its name and placement.
{0}: not in the binder, so it is created.
The {0} collision parts placing it are kept, and show the new mesh.
No collision part places it, so one is added.
Undoing restores the old meshes. Files that were created stay in the binders.
Overwrite
Replace the collision's mesh and write the binders into the project.
Cancel
Leave the collision as it is.
{0} has uncommitted edits in the Edit tab. Commit or discard them first.
{0} can't be overwritten: it doesn't have a single body with a compressed mesh.
The WALL files of {0}'s map couldn't be read, so its wall marks can't be cleared. Nothing was overwritten.
Overwrote {0} ({1} triangles).
The WALL files of {0}'s map couldn't be read, so its walls can't follow the rebuild. Nothing was committed.
Moved the wall marks of {0} to its rebuilt triangles: {1} of {2} WALL triangles, {3} of {4} NOJUMPWALL triangles.
